cards.subject: a calm biophilic bedroom for a child aged 2 to 5, with a flower-shaped birch craft table and a stack of bouclé poufs
cards.scene: A bright airy room with a wide-plank walnut floor. On an oval oat bouclé rug lie wax crayons in a wooden cup and an open drawing book, beside a small wooden watering can. On the RIGHT side wall, away from the mural: a low flower-shaped pale lacquered birch craft table 45 cm high with a stack of round bouclé poufs in ochre and barberry red, a round birch shelf with two sage ceramic pots of small ferns, and a framed leaf print above. Warm golden hour sunlight from a window on the RIGHT lies in long soft patches on the floor. A boy of about four in a soft oat knit sweater and light grey trousers stands on the floor in the middle of the room about two metres in front of the mural wall with his back to the camera, one arm raised and pointing up at the big balloon, his head tilted back to look up at it, his face turned away from the camera so no facial detail is visible, well away from the mural. Palette: pale birch, oat, ochre, barberry red and warm white.
cards.framing: Shot from the left part of the room at eye level, turned about 25 degrees toward the mural wall, so the RIGHT side wall is in view. The frame shows a floor-to-ceiling section of the mural wall around the two hot-air balloons: the ceiling line at the top of the frame, the skirting board and a strip of floor at the bottom; the mural continues beyond the frame edges at its true scale.

cards.subject: a sunny retro room for a schoolchild aged 6 to 10, with a low solid oak single bed with storage drawers and a low book shelf
cards.scene: A bright room with a cream and caramel checked linoleum floor. A rectangular crocheted play mat in mustard, cream and brown stripes lies by the bed with a wooden spinning top, a vintage tin car and a stack of board games. On the LEFT side wall, away from the mural: a low solid oak single bed 90 by 200 cm with under-bed drawers and butter yellow linen, beside it a 70 cm oak shelf with a few chapter books and a wooden pencil cup, and a small framed vintage map above. Crisp morning daylight from a window on the LEFT falls in clear bands across the floor. A sheer cream linen curtain hangs at the extreme right edge of the frame, close to the camera and slightly out of focus, as a foreground layer. Palette: honey oak, caramel, cream, mustard, sage and white.
cards.framing: Shot from the right part of the room at natural eye level, turned about 30 degrees toward the mural wall, so the LEFT side wall is in view. The frame shows a floor-to-ceiling section of the mural wall around the two hot-air balloons: the ceiling line at the top of the frame, the skirting board and a strip of floor at the bottom; the mural continues beyond the frame edges at its true scale. Nothing stands in front of the mural.

cards.subject: a playful fun-haus bedroom for a child aged 2 to 5, with a low birch Montessori floor bed and an arched cream cabinet
cards.scene: A light room with a pale ash herringbone floor. On a pill-shaped cream rug with wavy edges lie wax crayons in a wooden cup and an open drawing book. On the RIGHT side wall, away from the mural: a low solid birch Montessori floor bed with caramel-and-cream striped bedding and one blue cushion, an arch-fronted cream cabinet 55 cm high beside it, and a small framed vintage circus print. Warm golden hour sunlight from a window on the RIGHT lies in soft patches on the floor. At the left edge of the frame an open white door leads out of the room; a toddler girl of about two and a half in a blush knit sweater and cream trousers stands in the doorway with her back to the camera, one foot on the threshold, her face turned away from the camera so no facial detail is visible, well away from the mural. Palette: caramel, cream, brick, saturated blue and pale ash.
cards.framing: Shot from the left part of the room at eye level, turned about 25 degrees toward the mural wall, so the RIGHT side wall is in view. The frame shows a floor-to-ceiling section of the mural wall around the two hot-air balloons: the ceiling line at the top of the frame, the skirting board and a strip of floor at the bottom; the mural continues beyond the frame edges at its true scale.

clips.motion: The camera stays completely still on a tripod and does not move at all. A boy of about four in a soft oat knit sweater and light grey trousers stands with his back to the camera in front of the mural wall, his right arm already raised and pointing up at the big balloon, his head tilted back looking up at it. Slowly and calmly he takes one small step toward the wall while his arm stays raised and keeps pointing at the big balloon and his gaze stays on it. His body moves very little. Only the back of his head, his hair and his clothes are seen, and his head stays turned toward the wall. The rug, the toys and the room stay exactly as they are. The light stays constant.
clips.items: flower-shaped craft table, bouclé poufs, oval rug, wax crayons, drawing book, round shelf, picture frame and architecture

clips.motion: A smooth slow first-person walk-in: the camera advances steadily straight forward into the room at natural eye level, as if a person is slowly entering, with no sideways drift, no tilt and no rotation. The sheer cream curtain in the extreme foreground on the right leaves the frame as the camera advances past it, and the nearer objects shift more than the farther ones, giving a natural depth parallax.
clips.items: oak bed, storage drawers, low shelf, chapter books, pencil cup, crocheted mat, wooden toys, picture frame and architecture

clips.motion: The camera stays completely still on a tripod and does not move at all. A toddler girl of about two and a half in a blush knit sweater and cream trousers, standing in the open doorway at the left edge of the frame with her back to the camera, walks away from the camera through the doorway into the next room with calm unhurried steps and goes out of view; the white door stays exactly as it is, open, and she does not touch it. Her face is never visible to the camera, not even in profile: only the back of her head, her hair and her clothes are seen. She stays at the left edge of the frame, far from the two hot-air balloons, and never passes in front of the mural. The rug, the toys and the room stay exactly as they are. The warm light stays constant.
clips.items: birch floor bed, striped bedding, arched cabinet, pill-shaped rug, wax crayons, drawing book, picture frame and architecture
